title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' manuscripts, which follow La Longue Marche. The groups involved are as follows.
- π_{0,3}^ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}.
- π_{0,3}^~ = π_{0,3}^·{1,τ_∞} is its extension by an involution.
- M_{0,3}^{!~} is a group of 'admissible' automorphisms, presented by triples u = (α, β, f) subject to the loop equation. It is a GT-hat-like object, extended by the S_3-symmetries and by complex conjugation.
- N_{0,3}^{!~} is its quotient by inner automorphisms (π_{0,3}^ or C_{0,3}^+).
- There is a homomorphism M_{0,3}^{!~} → GL(2,Ẑ)'. This is the action on the abelianised fundamental group of the elliptic double cover (Legendre family / Γ(2) level).
- The 'Cases' are the fixed points of the S_3-action on P^1 \ {0,1,∞}, i.e. the elliptic (orbifold) points of M_{1,1}.
  - Case 1 (previous page) is the orbit {1/2, 2, -1}, which is j = 1728. There the relevant element σ_∞ satisfies σ_∞^2 = -1. The section κ_{1/2} of M → N factors through the normaliser of the non-split torus {tσ_∞+u : t^2+u^2 ∈ Ẑ^*} ≅ Ẑ[i]^*.
  - Case 2 (this page) is the orbit {-j, -j̄}, primitive sixth roots of unity, which is j = 0. The condition is β_0 = 1, equivalently α = f, ξ = fρ(f)^{-1}, equivalently [u, ρ] = 1 (103, 104), with ρ the order-3 symmetry.

The content of this page.
1. Let N_{0,3}^{!~}(-j̄) be the subgroup of u satisfying (103)/(104), i.e. those commuting with ρ. Its image in N_{0,3}^{!~} lies in the index-2 kernel of u ↦ ε_3(μ(u)) = ε_3(u), i.e. μ(u) ≡ 1 mod 3, where μ is the cyclotomic-type character.
2. Because the normalising element γ = α^{-1} lies in π_{0,3}^ exactly when ε_3 = 1 (eq. 105 of the previous page), one gets an isomorphism M_{0,3}^{!~}(-j̄) ≅ N_{0,3}^{!~}(-j̄). Inverting it gives a section k(-j̄): N(-j̄) → M(-j̄) ⊂ M_{0,3}^{!~} over this index-2 subgroup.
3. Composed with M → GL(2,Ẑ)', this section factors through the maximal torus {cρ+d : c, d ∈ Ẑ, c^2 - cd + d^2 ∈ Ẑ^*} ≅ Ẑ[ζ_3]^*. Here c^2 - cd + d^2 is the norm form for ρ^2 + ρ + 1 = 0. It lands in the torus itself, not just its normaliser, because u commutes with ρ.
4. Grothendieck conjectures that this is the only section (splitting) of M_{0,3}^{!~}, or even of M_{0,3}^!, with this property. This parallels the previous page's conjecture that κ_{1/2} is the only section factoring through a normaliser.
5. He announces that the property follows from an equivalent form of (103)(104) given by (79). The next page develops this as η σ_∞(η) = 1, ξ = fρ(f)^{-1}.

In modern terms: these are the profinite/GT analogues of the 'CM sections' at the orbifold points j = 0, 1728 of M_{1,1}. Their image in GL_2(Ẑ) is the Cartan torus of the CM order, exactly as the Galois representation on the Tate module of a CM elliptic curve factors through the Cartan of Z[ζ_3] or Z[i].
errors: The previous page's margin assigns the orbit {1/2, 2, -1} to j = 0. In fact λ ∈ {-1, 2, 1/2} gives j = 1728; j = 0 corresponds to λ = -ρ^{±1}, the case treated on this page. This page's -j̄ case is correctly the j = 0 point.

The machine transcription has 'normaliseur' and 'Borel[?]'. Since u commutes with ρ, the image lies in the centraliser, i.e. the maximal torus Ẑ[ρ]^*, not merely the normaliser. The manuscript appears to say 'tore maximal'.
Equation numbering in the transcription is off. The image shows (105)–(109) with overwritten numbers; the set {cρ+d} is labelled (109), not (108).

ideas.what: Subgroup of admissible (GT-type) automorphisms commuting with the order-3 symmetry ρ (stabiliser of the j=0 orbifold point), and its isomorphism with its image in the outer group on the index-2 subgroup μ ≡ 1 mod 3, giving a section k(-j̄)
ideas.modern_name: Sections of the profinite π_1 / GT extension attached to orbifold points; GT-hat preserving conjugacy classes of torsion in PSL_2(Ẑ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps (1990s, torsion elements and GT-hat); Nakamura on Galois action at CM/tangential points
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the S_3 and M_{1,1} orbifold structure but not these explicit sections

ideas.what: Image of the section in GL(2,Ẑ) lies in the non-split Cartan torus {cρ+d : c^2-cd+d^2 ∈ Ẑ^*} = Ẑ[ζ_3]^*
ideas.modern_name: CM / non-split Cartan image (analogue of the Galois representation of a CM elliptic curve with j=0)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical CM theory (Deuring, Serre); GT/elliptic analogues by Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto

ideas.what: Conjecture that this is the unique section/subgroup with this torus-factorisation property
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity/uniqueness of CM-type sections in GT-hat (anabelian section-type uniqueness)

missed.claim: Grothendieck conjectures that the section k(-j̄) attached to the j=0 orbifold point is the unique splitting of M_{0,3}^{!~} → N_{0,3}^{!~} (over μ ≡ 1 mod 3) whose image in GL(2,Ẑ) factors through the Ẑ[ζ_3]^* torus. The companion conjecture (previous page) says the same for κ_{1/2} at j=1728 with the Ẑ[i]^* normaliser. No proof is given.
missed.quote: Je suspecte que c'est le seul [scindage] de M^{!~}_{0,3} (voire de M^{!}_{0,3}) qui ait cette propriété.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a uniqueness/rigidity statement for 'CM sections' of GT-type groups. It is akin to section-conjecture-type questions at orbifold points of M_{1,1}. As far as I know it is not formulated in this form in the GT literature, which mostly treats conjugacy of torsion rather than uniqueness of sections with prescribed CM image.

missed.claim: This page explicitly links the stabilisers in GT-hat-type groups of the elliptic points j=0, 1728 with the CM structure: the Cartan tori Ẑ[ζ_3]^* and Ẑ[i]^* in GL_2(Ẑ). The link runs through the action on H_1 of the elliptic double cover, with the mod-3 character ε_3 cutting out an index-2 subgroup.
missed.quote: se factorise par le tore maximal de Gl(2,Ẑ)', formé des {cρ+d | c,d∈Ẑ, c²-cd+d²∈Ẑ^×}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a GT-side analogue of the CM Galois representation. It may be relevant to elliptic GT (Enriquez) and Hain–Matsumoto-type comparisons at CM points.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an interesting explicit unpublished computation of CM-type sections of a GT-like extension at the orbifold points, plus an open uniqueness conjecture. The underlying phenomena (torsion conjugacy in GT, CM Cartan images) are known in spirit, so a specialist would not be very surprised.
transcription_corrections: 'se factorise par le Borel[?] normaliseur de Gl(2,Ẑ)'' should read roughly 'se factorise par le tore maximal ρ? de Gl(2,Ẑ)''. The word 'maximal' is visible at the start of that line.
'Je suspecte que c'est le seul sous-groupe[?]' is more likely 'c'est la seule scindage' (splitting/section), parallel to the previous page.
Equation labels: the map u ↦ ε_3(μ(u)) gives (105); the iso is (106) or (107); the diagram is (108); the torus set is (109). The transcription's numbering is shifted.
Left top margin: 'NB M^{!~}_{0,3}(-j̄) est stable par (103),(104) [?]', partly illegible.
Bottom-left margin is roughly 'corollaire, pour mieux voir que tout à l'heure…'; uncertain.
